nodes.name: Hydrothermal synthesis
nodes.procedure: 24 mmol Ni(NO3)2·6H2O and 24 mmol Na2MoO4·2H2O were dissolved into 360 mL deionized water and formed a transparent green solution. The solution was then transferred into a 500-mL Teflon-lined autoclave, and four pieces of nickel foam were added. After reaction at 120°C for 6 h, the nickel foam samples were taken out, washed, and vacuum dried, and NiMoO4·×H2O arrays were obtained.
nodes.source_text: Scalable Synthesis of NiMoO4 × H2O Arrays... After reaction at 120 °C for 6 h, the nickel foam samples were taken out, washed, and vacuum dried, and NiMoO4·×H2O arrays were obtained.

nodes.name: Calcination
nodes.procedure: After calcination of NiMoO4·×H2O nanowire arrays at 550°C, NiMoO4 nanowire arrays were fabricated.
nodes.source_text: after calcination of NiMoO4·×H2O nanowire arrays at 550 °C, NiMoO4 nanowire arrays with a mass loading of ∼2.6 mg cm−2 were fabricated.

nodes.name: Anodic oxidation reconstruction
nodes.procedure: The anodic oxidation process on NiMoO4·×H2O precursor was carried out in the standard three-electrode system in 1 M KOH... After carrying out CV tests in 0.924-1.724 V_RHE at a scan rate of 50 mV s^-1 for 30 cycles, black CR-NiOOH nanowire/nanosheet arrays were obtained with a mass loading of ∼1.2 mg cm^-2.
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of CR-NiOOH Nanowire/Nanosheet Arrays... After carrying out CV tests in 0.924-1.724 V_RHE at a scan rate of 50 mV s^-1 for 30 cycles, black CR-NiOOH nanowire/nanosheet arrays were obtained.

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4·xH2O nanowires are monocrystalline with smooth surface confirmed by TEM imaging.
nodes.evidence_snippet: These nanowires are monocrystalline with a smooth surface, confirmed by transmission electron microscopy (TEM) imaging and the corresponding selected area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern (Figure S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: Powder XRD pattern of NiMoO4·xH2O nanowires similar to reported CoMoO4·0.75H2O analog.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the powder X-ray diffraction (XRD) pattern is similar to that of the reported analog CoMoO4·0.75H2O.

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH nanowire interconnected by sub-5-nm ultrasmall nanoparticles resulting in ~5-nm nanopores.
nodes.evidence_snippet: HAADF-STEM imaging clearly demonstrates its morphological characterization... Such a nanowire is interconnected by sub-5-nm ultrasmall nanoparticles (NPs), resulting in visible interspaces with ~5-nm nanopores accessible to electrolytes.

nodes.characterization_summary: All interplanar spacings of NPs within CR-NiOOH nanowire indexed to NiOOH planes: 0.158 nm (220), 0.208 nm (210), 0.213 nm (111), 0.240 nm (011), 0.248 nm (101).
nodes.evidence_snippet: All interplanar spacings of NPs within the nanowire are well indexed to the planes of NiOOH (Figure 2B). The exposed interplanar spacings of 0.158, 0.208, 0.213, 0.240, and 0.248 nm can be well assigned to the (220), (210), (111), (011), and (101) planes of orthorhombic NiOOH.

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH shows O/Ni atomic ratio 2.05 and Mo content 0.1 at.% confirming pure NiOOH phase.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the O/Ni atomic ratio is 2.05 from the corresponding energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) spectroscopy spectrum (Figure 2C), which further demonstrates the pure phase of CR-NiOOH. In addition, negligible content (0.1 atomic percentage [at.%]) of the Mo element suggests its absence within the nanowire.

nodes.characterization_summary: CR-NiOOH shows Raman peaks at 474 cm⁻¹ (eg bending) and 554 cm⁻¹ (A1g stretching) of Ni-O vibrations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only two Raman peaks at 474 and 554 cm⁻¹ belonging to the eg bending and the A1g stretching vibration of Ni-O in NiOOH24 are observed (Figure S4E).

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern confirms low-crystalline and polycrystalline characteristics of CR-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: It displays low-crystalline and polycrystalline characteristics confirmed by the SAED pattern (Figure S4D).

nodes.characterization_summary: NiMoO4 shows only 7-nm-thick NiOOH shell with inner continuous lattice fringes indexed to NiMoO4 (JCPDS 86-0361) planes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Only an 7-nm-thick NiOOH layer forms, and the inner continuous lattice fringes covering dozens of nanometers are indexed to the planes of NiMoO4 (JCPDS 86-0361) (Figure 2H).

nodes.characterization_summary: STEM elemental mapping confirms core-shell NiMoO4@NiOOH structure with no Mo signal in 7-nm NiOOH shell.
nodes.evidence_snippet: STEM element mapping further confirms the core-shell structure as undetected Mo signals in the shell region (Figure 2I).

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ EIS shows charge transfer resistance Rct of NiMoO4·xH2O/NF decreases from 34 Ω to 6.5 Ω after CV activation indicating faster charge transfer of CR-NiOOH.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Ex situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) results from the same electrode show that the charge transport resistance (Rct) decreased significantly from 34 to 6.5 ohm (Ω), indicating faster charge transfer of CR-NiOOH (Figure 3B).

nodes.characterization_summary: Potential-dependent in situ Raman shows NiMoO4·xH2O reconstructs to CR-NiOOH with peaks at 474 and 554 cm⁻¹ while NiMoO4 remains almost unchanged.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Potential-dependent in situ Raman spectra of (A) NiMoO4$xH2O$ and (B) NiMoO4 a 0.924-1.824 V_RHE with the interval voltage of 50 mV in 1 M KOH, showing that NiMoO4$xH2O$ gradually reconstructs to CR-NiOOH but NiMoO4 is almost unchanged.

nodes.characterization_summary: Ex situ XRD shows disappearance of NiMoO4·xH2O peaks at ~27.3° and 29.8° demonstrating structural crack and amorphization.
nodes.evidence_snippet: With the ex situ XRD measurement, disappearance of the representative peaks at ~27.3° and 29.8°, which belong to NiMoO4$xH2O$, demonstrates its structural crack and amorphization (Figure S11A).
